citations.review_text:
One of my favorite fps games of all time. Sadly its pretty dead nowadays, 2 lobbys full tho. 
Not sure how/what the card rarity affects but for new players getting them will be hard since getting currency for them takes a while and old players have quite insane/good cards for the characters already.

Fun as f despite all and honestly easily beats modern games by miles in term of fun. What a hidden gem!

Dirty Bomb is one of the earliest attempts to capitalize on Valve's success by just copying their ideas and making something quote unquote "new" from the bones of TF2 and the guns from Counter-Strike. Throw in some abilities here and there, and a live service model, and you got Dirty Bomb.

So first off, the game is BEYOND dead. No one is playing, so outright I can't recommend it. I CAN'T recommend someone bother trying to play a game that doesn't exist anymore.

I can't really give a strong description of the game because I have only played it solo, but I kind of instinctively don't like it. Oh, login bonus, huh? First match of the day bonus, is that so? Oh, I need to buy characters and so on? In-game free money system huh? Boy, I sure would love to play what is trying to be a competitive shooter where I have to unlock the content to play the game.

The structure of this kind of live service game is just outdated in my opinion, League of Legends has the same kind of problem but the thing there is that game is from like 2011 and is one of the progenitors of all this nonsense we have to put up with today. Me, I'm a DotA 2 kind of person and I appreciate that more. Give me everything I need to play the game and get your other nonsense out of here - if you want me to pay anything to you for your free game, it better be exclusively cosmetics.

So yeah, even if there were people playing this game now, today, I still wouldn't play it. Sorry Splash Damage, Brink sucked.

I've seen other people be all nostalgic and wistful up in here about Enemy Territory and stuff, but I have to ask, how many people still at this company actually were still working at Splash Damage at the point they were making this? Was this their like desperate attempt to break into being an 'indie' (Nexon, lol, lmao), dev who plays by their own rules, like Warframe or Path of Exile? Well, I guess not because they chose, Nexon, which is the kiss of death for a lot of sensible people because they know wha…

claims.claim: Reviewers note the complete absence of bot support, preventing them from playing real matches due to the lack of players.

citations.review_text: And to think, a decade ago I was called ******* and many such names for suggesting bot support.... Probably woulda helped now that its dead. LoL Rip bozo

The release of Dirty Bomb was basically a first time when Splash Damage managed to make their gameplay formula work so that people actually played their game. Their previous multiplayer shooters like Enemy Territory: Quake Wars and Brink also had same gameplay where one team had to complete specific tasks on the map and another team had to prevent it but both those games were pretty much dead at launch. Brink actually felt like unfinished game so there it was understandable. But it was more strange story with Enemy Territory: Quake Wars. The reason there was that market trends back then were just different, probably. So, Dirty Bomb actually received some recognition and popularity. Perhaps it wouldn't be so if not Steam and social networks, as it became easier to attract audience to your project in 2010s. Well, anyway now this game is dead and Splash Damage do not work on their own IPs anymore. Such a shame. There is also no bots, so I was even unable to actually play any real match. Still, I mark this review as positive and I wish Splash Damage success in their future projects.

Overwatch really just siphoned all the attention in this genre, didn't it? And Dirty Bomb released before it!

I first played this during its open beta in 2015 for a couple hours, but I didn't fully understand it at the time to keep with it. Revisiting it in 2025, now that I've gained the skills for this genre from hundreds of hours in Overwatch, I had a pretty good time with it. I can usually find one or two full servers of 14 players every evening. I'm not that good, but I still have fun getting assists and using my abilities to help my team win objectives.

Some downsides are the movement being very snappy and quick, which personally makes it very difficult for me to aim and kill people. And you have to unlock most characters and preset weapon loadouts, seemingly very slowly. So, it's a bit weird starting out, especially when you don't know what kindof heroes and weapons you think you'd like.

Not sure it'll hold my attention for too long, but it's a good hero shooter and it's free.

citations.review_text: i cant even express how good this game is to you guys, its overly too good to be true, its late for those who not know this games before, but this game has the potential to be greatness, powerful skill,  lore, interest builds with same character with different type of play to master. the movement is smooth and ahead of its time and only for 6gb storage. i still remembered years ago in 2015 i was happy, everyday after school i will visit internet cafe just to download this game and play with online friends i made along the way of playing this game. we surprised each others with new movement tech and builds we have never seen before. One days one of us interest in sth else because matching takes too much time, we have come to realize that players are leaving the game so much that's only few hundreds players globally, then below hundreds and then there's only 10 lefts, those 10 randoms were playing with each others in their private room all my friends offline and disappears, i have no one to play with so i just stayed in the training room to practice parkour for a game i know that no one will ever play with me again.

Honest review after 70+ hours

[h3] Pros [/h3]
[+] The game is complitely F2P, skins can be earned while playing by unlocking chests with the earned currency
[+] Tons of fun characters with unique abilties and different classes/play-style
[+] Small community with around 50-55 players online everyday, kinda chill and friendly (especially those in the discord server), game vets sometimes helpful
[+] Low end game tho

[h3] Cons [/h3]
[-] Most of the community is pretty toxic, peoples teamkill if u do something wrong, newbies are sometimes insulted when they plays or even kicked from the lobbies; if u are new in the game DONT listen to those players and play the game freely.
[-] Only few servers fully popolated and the others are empty, so big waiting time for those full servers
[-] Splash Damage took weeks to realise that the game was offline last time the server went off (they doesent care at all); the game is pretty much abandoned by the devs.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is abandoned by developers and no longer receives updates.

citations.review_text: This was an amazing game back in the day. My old account probably had 700+ hours on it. But now that the devs abandoned the game as well as the community, the only players now are those who never stopped. It's their stomping grounds, and its not friendly to either new players or rusty vets like myself looking for a shot of nostalgia. If this game had a resurgence of players, new and old, it could be amazing again with players of all skill levels simply enjoying the game. But as it is now, there's no longer any meaningful enjoyment to be found for those not already sunken deep in the abandoned trenches of Dirty Bomb.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the loadout card system as random, leaving players with no direct control over weapon and perk combinations.

citations.review_text:
man i remember this game with a slight degree of fondness... mostly because it was one of the handful of games which ran well on my old, bargain-bin desktop.

yet somehow it runs like utter dogwater on even vaguely modern hardware. yeah i don't think the game engine has any concept of what an RTX 2060 even [i]is[/i].

I wouldn't recommend it in its current state. 

Hell, I wouldn't recommend in its heyday. 

Largely because of the grind. Yeah the reason I didn't stick to it and chose Warframe as my poison of choice was that to unlock a new hero ('Merc') you'd need between 30 to 40 thousand in-game credits. You would get somewhere in the range of 100 (yeah let's say 100 to make the maths easier) per match... which comes up to needing 300 to 400 matches to unlock a 'Merc'. Unless you pay real money. 

the game was never good enough for me to consider paying real money

Coupled that with the inherent randomness of the entire 'loadout card' system (you could get packs, which would net you a card, which was a randomly-generated assortment of primary, secondary, melee weapon and a couple perks), which meant you had absolutely NO control in fine-tuning your gameplay... 

Yeah it largely turned me off, less than 40 hours in. I just hopped back in right before writing the review, to see just how dead this game really is. 

Really, the solution, to me, seems damn simple: just do away with the God-forsaken 'loadout card' system and divide the 'Merc' unlock costs by a factor of 10. But, well, I don't make the decisions here and those who [i]were[/i] making them decided to just ax the game so here we are!

One of my most favorite releases from Splash Damage. Only downfall was the card system. A balanced progression system with paid skins or something of that nature would have sustained this game better.

Community is mostly garbage, predominantly toxic player base, no updates, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ near abandoned servers. Hard to pickup as a new player because the roughly 100 people that are still active are a bunch of die hard level 100+ douche bags who ***** , kick people, and rage quit lobbies when someone without 1000+ in game hours joins up. 

That being said, I love this game, I've been playing for 10 years. In its peak it was a FANTASTIC game. No pay to win, fun maps, many characters with different play styles for each. It was and is still one of my favorite games ever. When you get a good, full lobby, its a blast. Sad to see it go the way it has. I really hope it revives one day.

I would recommend it, but it's a dead game.
Sucks, it really had potential to be amazing.

Look, I don't know how many people are gonna see this, but I just have to give my love to this game. The amount of character and soul that was poured into it is truly commendable, and even seven years after it stopped receiving updates there are still a handful of community servers running where you can find a- usually quite small- match. 

Dirty Bomb came and went too soon, but for myself and everyone else that played while it was in active development- and those that still do, it was and is a bright spot in competitive multiplayer.

For some reason I hadn't left a review for this game. Well I have 1500 hours in it (and it wasn't free back then!), for me it -was- the best FPS. I love Splash Damage and my fav FPSes were by them: Wolf ET & Quake Wars (Brink was too slow though). 

It's very sad that this game didn't meet its public. Perhaps the genre itself has died, in favor of Battle Royale games. 
Last time I played, and it was some time ago, there were only a few servers left. Still, I haven't found any better FPS yet. But it's safe to say that this game will never have a second (or third) life, sadly.

this game is dead. and servers are filled with <40 players 800+ level guys playin at night. 
dont play or install this game. go to tf2, overwatch or finals or paladins. this is the game that created all of them

Dirty Bomb is just another online first person shooter. Is this game any different from other FPS’? Absolutely not. There are several aspects of the game that are actually worse. Let me start from the fact that the game has been abandoned for 6 years now. When you launch the game and load to main menu, it may seem like the game is still alive as you are bombarded with updates and other news related to the game. The moment you actually click on one of those news or updates, you are gonna see the year of 2019 everywhere. 

The game being abandoned can also be visible by the number of active players (less than 100 players login on a daily basis) and the quality of such players. There are only a handful of people left that still play the game and they are as toxic as it gets. The chat is full of disrespectful comments, insults, bullying and trash talk. People are more focused on fighting on the chat than fighting in-game. I didn’t like seeing this so I started muting other players. After a few matches I already had a majority of the server muted but only in theory. You see, the mute works but only for the match it was applied in. When you start another match you are going to see that the players you previously muted show as muted but you can still see what they are writing. If you wanna keep these people muted, you have to go out of your way at the beginning of every match to unmute and mute them again. What is even worse is the fact that mute doesn’t apply to in-game quick chat commands. Despite muting someone, you will still see all the quick chat messages that, of course, are sent in an insulting manner like spamming “Nice shot!” after someone misses an ability and dies. The game doesn’t give you an option to turn off the chat so you are forced to endure that constant toxicity for your whole experience with the game. Another thing I would like to mention are cheaters. So far, I have only come across two that weren’t trying to hide it and were very obvious about it. I…

citations.review_text: valla bu oyunun neden bu kadar az bilindiğine hayret ediyorum, piyasadaki en hızlı ve en yetenek gerektiren shooterlardan biri net. o parkur mekanikleri, zıplayarak duvarlardan sekip adam vurmak falan inanılmaz bi özgürlük hissi veriyor. karakterlerin her birinin kendine has bir yeteneği ve görevi olması takım oyununu çok ön plana çıkarıyor. öyle sadece mermi yağdırıp geçemiyorsun, düzgün bir taktik ve doğru zamanda kullanılan yetenekler maçı döndürüyor resmen. vuruş hissiyatı aşırı keskin ve tatmin edici, tam bir "skill-based" ortamı var yani bileğine güvenen buyursun gelsin. grafik tarzı da o hafif kıyamet sonrası londra atmosferini çok iyi yansıtmış. bedava olmasına rağmen p2w olayına girmemeleri de büyük artı. hızlı, aksiyonu bol ve gerçekten rekabetçi bir fps arıyorsanız kesinlikle bi şans verin, pişman etmez.

The game is dead now. The devs of the game wanted to focus on gun-play, with abilities at the side, which guided their balance decisions that kneecapped the fun out of the game in my opinion. At the time it felt they were nerfing certain mercs just because of me, and all the fun things I could do. But even as the game remains today, it is actually fun, and the true fun of this game is found from the correct use of the merc abilities, followed by the fast acrobatic movement across the map, and the gun play as the finishing touch. It is kind of like Wolfenstein: Enemy Territory, set in a nuclear devasted London. So, what keeps the game alive even today is thanks to community servers, and there is at least one populated server roughly at every hour of the day. So give it a try. You can earn in game credits, unlock mercs when they are not in the free rotation, buy and roll the roulette wheel for loadout cards that either look prettier or suit better your game style. It is entirely free to play. 

I do not say it is cheater free, because there are sad excuses who do cheat even in a dead game. But, the odds are you do not run into them, and when you do, you can just leave and join a different server.

Used to be a great game, still has it's charm. It has everything a f2p shooter needs - fun objective modes, good map designs, accurate gunplay, fun abilities (though some feel a little out of place, especially the newer mercs like guardian) and great movement. There's no more microtransactions and you can get everything in the game with only credits, which you gain by playing over time. They left us a satisfactory state of the game to play.

 One of my favorite parts of the game is the ability to chain together long jumps and wall jumps as ANY character, as well as great gunplay. This makes for a game where you can play any merc and you'll be fine, but you better switch to medic or ammo if you team doesn't have one or you will probably lose. Good thing you can bring 3 different mercs into battle at a time.

If you're coming back after a long time, expect the same amounts of fun and satisfaction in the gameplay mechanics. If you're completely new, stick around and learn the game before you throw it in the trash. Try new mercs and see what you like. The game promises a good time if you can find a lobby.

Used to be a great game, still has it's charm. It has everything a f2p shooter needs - fun objective modes, good map designs, accurate gunplay, fun abilities (though some feel a little out of place, especially the newer mercs like guardian) and great movement. There's no more microtransactions and you can get everything in the game with only credits, which you gain by playing over time. They left us a satisfactory state of the game to play.

 One of my favorite parts of the game is the ability to chain together long jumps and wall jumps as ANY character, as well as great gunplay. This makes for a game where you can play any merc and you'll be fine, but you better switch to medic or ammo if you team doesn't have one or you will probably lose. Good thing you can bring 3 different mercs into battle at a time.

If you're coming back after a long time, expect the same amounts of fun and satisfaction in the gameplay mechanics. If you're completely new, stick around and learn the game before you throw it in the trash. Try new mercs and see what you like. The game promises a good time if you can find a lobby.

Hard to pickup as a new player because the roughly 100 people that are still active are a bunch of die hard level 100+ douche bags who ***** , kick people, and rage quit lobbies when someone without 1000+ in game hours joins up. 

That being said, I love this game, I've been playing for 10 years. In its peak it was a FANTASTIC game. No pay to win, fun maps, many characters with different play styles for each. It was and is still one of my favorite games ever. When you get a good, full lobby, its a blast. Sad to see it go the way it has. I really hope it revives one day.

The game is dead now. The devs of the game wanted to focus on gun-play, with abilities at the side, which guided their balance decisions that kneecapped the fun out of the game in my opinion. At the time it felt they were nerfing certain mercs just because of me, and all the fun things I could do. But even as the game remains today, it is actually fun, and the true fun of this game is found from the correct use of the merc abilities, followed by the fast acrobatic movement across the map, and the gun play as the finishing touch. It is kind of like Wolfenstein: Enemy Territory, set in a nuclear devasted London. So, what keeps the game alive even today is thanks to community servers, and there is at least one populated server roughly at every hour of the day. So give it a try. You can earn in game credits, unlock mercs when they are not in the free rotation, buy and roll the roulette wheel for loadout cards that either look prettier or suit better your game style. It is entirely free to play. 

I do not say it is cheater free, because there are sad excuses who do cheat even in a dead game. But, the odds are you do not run into them, and when you do, you can just leave and join a different server.
